transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because after losing a job opportunity at an arts nonprofit that I was really counting on, I feel like I’ve been reacting badly to everything. I just feel completely unable to cope with what's happening in my life right now.
How long have you been feeling this way, and besides the reaction to losing the job opportunity, have you also had low mood or worry most days for at least two weeks?

It’s been about two months now, starting just a few weeks after I found out the job fell through. I definitely feel low and anxious most days, but it's completely tied to this situation and everything being up in the air with my loans and lease. I was doing totally fine before this happened, so it doesn't feel like a separate, ongoing issue.
Since this started, have your symptoms felt out of proportion to the stressor or caused major problems at work, school, or in relationships beyond what you would expect from this situation?

Yes, my reactions feel completely overwhelming and way out of proportion; even a simple email from my landlord or a text about a gig makes me shut down, cry, and just scroll on my phone. Because of this, I've lost out on paid work, stopped showing up to my improv group, and let my lease and student loan emails pile up to a really scary point.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living since this started?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. I just feel incredibly overwhelmed and stressed by how quickly everything changed, and I'm really struggling to cope with the sudden disruption to my plans.
Have these symptoms started to improve as you’ve begun adjusting to the job loss and the related stress, or do they feel just as intense now as when they first began?

They haven't improved at all and feel just as intense now as they did when this first started two months ago. Since my job, lease, and loans are still completely up in the air, I still feel totally derailed, though I hope this reaction won't last forever once I finally get a stable plan in place.
Have you ever had a similar reaction to a major stressor before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this overwhelmed after a life event?
No, I haven't really experienced a reaction this severe or overwhelming in the past. This level of struggle feels completely new to me and is tied specifically to my current situation.
Have the stressors that triggered this started to resolve, or are they still ongoing and unresolved?

No, they are completely unresolved and still ongoing right now. I still don't have a stable job, and my lease renewal and student loan situations are completely up in the air. Everything feels so uncertain, which is why I feel so stuck and unable to move forward.
Did this reaction begin within a few months of the stressful event, and is it mainly tied to that event rather than happening on its own?

Yes, it started within just a few weeks of finding out the job fell through, and I was doing completely fine before that. This overwhelming reaction is definitely tied directly to losing that position and the sudden instability of my life right now. It's not something that would have just happened on its own.
Since this started, have you had any intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about losing the job opportunity or the related stress?

No, I haven't experienced any nightmares, flashbacks, or intrusive memories about losing the job. While I feel extremely stressed and tend to avoid dealing with things, I don't have those specific types of symptoms.
Have the stress-related problems started to ease at all as you adjust, or do they stay severe even when you are away from the stressors?

No, they haven't eased at all because the stressors—like my job situation, housing, and student loans—are still completely unresolved and constantly on my mind. I've been feeling this way for about two months now, but it's entirely tied to everything being so up in the air right now. I really hope that once I get a stable job or a new plan sorted out, this reaction won't go on forever.
Has the main stressor been resolved yet, or are you still feeling this way even after things have settled down?

No, the main stressors are still very much unresolved and things haven't settled down at all. My job situation, student loans, and lease renewal are all still completely up in the air, which is why I've been struggling to cope for the last two months. I feel like my reaction is entirely tied to these ongoing, unsettled issues.
Has your stress reaction continued even when you are away from the job, lease, and loan issues, or does it mainly happen when you are dealing with those problems directly?

Even when I try to distract myself, any tiny reminder like a text or an email immediately triggers my chest tightness and makes me shut down, so it's deeply tied to those unresolved problems. It feels like I can't escape it because everything is still so up in the air right now. I really feel that once these specific situations are finally resolved, this intense reaction will finally stop.
Have your symptoms continued for more than 6 months after the stressful event, or have they mainly been present only while the job, lease, and loan problems are still unresolved?

No, it has only been about two months since the job fell through, so it hasn't been six months yet. My reactions are entirely tied to everything currently being up in the air with my job, lease, and loans. I really believe that once I finally sort these unresolved issues out, this reaction won't go on forever.
Have your symptoms been present for less than 6 months since the stressful event, or have they continued for longer than 6 months?

They have been present for less than six months—it has only been about two months since the job fell through. I feel like this reaction is directly tied to everything being so up in the air right now. I don't expect it to go on forever once I can finally sort out a stable job or living situation.
Have these symptoms gone away within 6 months after the stressful event, or are they still going on because the stressor is ongoing?

They are still going on because the stressor is very much ongoing and unresolved; it's only been about two months since the job fell through. I'm still actively dealing with the uncertainty of my housing, upcoming loan payments, and not having a stable job. I really feel like these feelings are tied directly to everything being so up in the air right now rather than being a permanent issue.

Besides feeling overwhelmed by this situation, have you also been having persistent low mood or anxiety that feels out of proportion to the stressor, or is it mainly a reaction to the job, housing, and loan problems?

It is definitely a direct reaction to the job, housing, and loan stressors rather than a separate, long-standing issue. Everything just feels completely up in the air right now, which is why I'm reacting this way. I really believe that once I get a stable job or a solid plan sorted out, this won't last forever.
Do you feel your reaction is much more intense than what most people would have in the same situation, and is it making it hard for you to function day to day?

Yes, it definitely feels way more intense than it should be; even a minor text or email makes my chest tighten, and I just shut down and cry instead of dealing with things. It's completely disrupted my daily life, causing me to lose out on paid gigs, stop going to my regular improv group, and let my lease and student loan emails pile up to a scary point.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than 6 months since the stressful event started, or have they only been present for a shorter time?

No, they have only been present for a shorter time—it's been about two months since the job fell through. I feel like this reaction is entirely tied to my current unstable situation rather than being a long-standing issue.
Has the stressful situation started to improve at all, or are the job, housing, and loan problems still ongoing and unresolved?

No, it hasn't improved at all and everything is still completely unresolved and up in the air. I still don't have a stable job, and my lease and student loan issues are just continuing to pile up. I feel like this reaction is going to persist until I can finally get these practical matters sorted out.
Have you been feeling mainly sad or anxious, or have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

It is really a mix of both. I feel highly anxious and overwhelmed, to the point where my chest tightens and I just cry when trying to face daily tasks, but I've also lost the motivation to do things I used to love. I've completely stopped attending my regular improv meet-ups and backed out of organizing community events that I used to thrive on.
Since this started, have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or any thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to die at all. Even though I feel incredibly overwhelmed, stressed, and unable to cope with everything that's happening right now, I've never had those kinds of thoughts.
Have the job, housing, or loan problems started to improve at all, or are they still ongoing and unresolved right now?

No, they are still completely unresolved and ongoing, with the job loss, upcoming student loans, and my lease renewal still totally up in the air. That is why I feel so overwhelmed and stuck right now, as everything is just suspended. I really hope that once I can finally sort out a stable job or housing plan, this reaction will begin to improve.
Have you noticed any persistent problems with concentration, sleep, or appetite since this started, or is it mainly the emotional reaction and difficulty coping with the stressor?

It's definitely more of the emotional reaction and feeling completely derailed by the stress. I haven't really had persistent issues with my sleep, appetite, or concentration, but I just feel so overwhelmed that I shut down, cry, and avoid my emails and commitments because I can't cope with the situation.
